content: When initiating or discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, such as clarithromycin, it is essential to closely monitor levels of 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact parathyroid hormone (PTH), and serum calcium concentrations. This is because clarithromycin can increase the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments, such as reducing the cannabidiol dose, should be considered when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of capmatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Similarly, vonoprazan decreases the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, which applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cariprazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of cariprazine is required when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the dosage modification section in the drug monograph for guidance. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of cefdinir, cefditoren, cefoxitin, cefpodoxime, and cefuroxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents like clarithromycin may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments, such as increasing the dose of CYP3A4 substrates, may be necessary when co-administered with cenobamate. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ceritinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cevimeline, chlordiazepoxide, and cholic acid by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. For cholic acid, avoid concomitant use of bile salt efflux pump (BSEP) inhibitors, as this may exacerbate the accumulation of conjugated bile salts in the liver, leading to clinical symptoms. If co-administration is necessary, monitor serum transaminases and bilirubin. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ciclesonide (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Reduce the cilostazol dose to 50 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of citalopram by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of clevidipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Increased effects of calcium channel blockers, such as clevidipine, may lead to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of clonazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of clonidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, so caution is necessary with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Vonoprazan decreases the levels or effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. This may reduce plasma concentrations of the active metabolite of clopidogrel, leading to decreased platelet inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of clorazepate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. As vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, caution is advised with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens (oral) by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. However, clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens (oral and vaginal) by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cortisone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin increases the levels of crizotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. ECG monitoring is recommended, especially with drugs that may prolong the QT interval. Crofeler increases the levels of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Crofeler has the potential to inhibit CYP3A4 at concentrations expected in the gut but is unlikely to inhibit it systemically due to minimal absorption. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Vonoprazan also increases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. As vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, caution is necessary with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of dabigatran by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. For atrial fibrillation, avoid co-administration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if creatinine clearance (CrCl) is less than 30 mL/min. For deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE) treatment, avoid co-administration if CrCl is less than 50 mL/min. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. As vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, caution is necessary with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary.
